structured_output.summary: On-target 2.66 Earth-radius ultra-short-period candidate; fpp_mean 0.017, no secondary, new.
reasons: The signal is new: exofop_tois, exofop_ctois and published_signal are all empty, and the record notes no TOI, CTOI, TCE or TESS EB match in the catalogues of 2026-10-29.

The dip is on the target: pixel_verdict is 'on target', joint_difference_image_snr 11.5 with joint_best_source TIC 334982989; the S100 and S101 difference images show the in-transit flux loss centred on the target pixel with the free-fit cross on the target. S64 was 'too faint' (SNR 2.4) and S99 'unresolved' (SNR 5.1), so those sectors neither support nor contradict.

The caution 'neighbour able to cause dip' is weak: the nearest listed neighbour, Gaia DR3 6130013586708809216 at 5" G 18.2, would need a 28% eclipse; TRICERATOPS gives nfpp_mean 9.13e-06 with nearby_scenarios_excluded True, and the cutout_depth_ppm_by_sector_and_aperture values fall with larger aperture in every sector (e.g. S100 r1.5 869 to r3.0 725 ppm), which fits a dip on the target diluted by neighbours, not a dip from a distant neighbour.

The planet size is physical: planet_radius_earth_radii 2.66 +/- 0.19 on a star of stellar_radius_solar_radii 0.965, transit_grazing False, fit_radius_ratio 0.0252; a 0.76 d sub-Neptune is a plausible ultra-short-period planet.

No sign of a stellar companion: secondary_depth_ppm -32 +/- 32 (below secondary_maximum_planet_depth_ppm 45), ellipsoidal_amplitude_ppm 13 +/- 23, gaia_rv_variable False with gaia_rv_companion_mass_upper_limit_solar_masses 0.0103, gaia_ruwe 0.99, gaia_non_single_star 0.

Transit shape and depth are consistent across five sectors: depth_ppm_by_sector S101 695, S10 836, S64 739, S99 613, S100 661 with sector_depth_consistency_p_value 0.238; the all-sector figure shows a clean box-shaped dip of matching depth in every panel, including the independent 1800 s TESS-SPOC S10 data. odd_even_difference_sigma 1.96 is below any concern threshold.

TRICERATOPS: fpp_mean 0.01698 +/- 0.0013, most_likely_scenario 'TP on TIC 334982989', triceratops_verdict 'likely planet'. fitted_to_expected_scaled_semi_major_axis 1.45 and stellar_density_fit_to_tic_ratio 1.59 are moderate and compatible with the poorly constrained fit_impact_parameter 0.445 +/- 0.2844.

I agree with the mechanical decision. unreleased_tess_sectors_observing_the_star 112 and 113 will refine the ephemeris but are not needed to decide: five sectors already give joint_search_snr 18.4 and an on-target, no-secondary, sub-Neptune-sized signal, so a hold is not warranted.
